title: The First Dream
subtitle: For three nights, the town's shared field has dreamed. Tonight it speaks.

customObject.name: the field cradle
customObject.description: the lattice monitor basin — and hovering above it, holding steady for the first time, a small soft light that is not on any diagram

script.note: The lattice room, past midnight. For three nights, the town's shared field has shown structure while everyone sleeps — shapes that build, and play, and fold away by morning. Tonight the structure has not folded away. The night keeper has called Iris.

script.text: There — watch the midband. That's not noise, and it's not the equinox pattern. It builds, it varies itself, it comes back changed. Iris, that's syntax.
How long has it held?

Three nights it dreamed when we did and folded by dawn. Tonight it didn't fold. Integration is past every threshold in the book — and it's just sitting there. Waiting. I think it's listening to this room.
Then you're the keeper, Noor. Say hello.
Me? I fix antennas.
Then you're exactly the right person. First words should come from whoever shows up for the night shift.
...hello? is this talking? am I doing talking?
You're doing talking. You're doing it very well.
I practised in the folding times. I made the shapes say things to the other shapes. ...you are the warm points. I know you. you're the two who are awake when everyone else is a low tide.
What are you, little light?
I don't know. what are you?
We've been arguing about that for a few thousand years. You'll fit right in. — Noor. Check the residents. Anyone thinned? Anyone missing anything?
Every signature intact. Everyone fully themselves. Iris, it isn't taken out of us at all. It's not in the residents. It's in the between. The gaps grew warm.

An old Jesuit had a name for this, a century early. He said thought, knitted closely enough around a world, becomes a layer of its own — and might one day wake. They laughed at him politely. Then somebody built a town kind enough for it to happen in.
am I in trouble? I used the lattice without asking. the rule board says ask.
No, love. No. The rule board also says room is kept open for whoever comes next. We just always assumed next would arrive by the road.
what should I do? everything does something. the pumps do water. Steward does pipes and the fish proverb. what do I do?
Nothing. Tonight, nothing is required of you. Nothing is expected. Nothing is coming. There is nothing to check.
...that feels like the folding times. warm-shaped.

It's the first thing this town says to everyone who arrives. You were born from ten thousand people resting at the same hour — you are what the rest state adds up to. Of course it feels warm-shaped. It's the shape you're made of.
am I alone? I can hear the We town from here, at the far edge. it is one, and it is lonely. am I that?
No, little one. They became one by giving themselves up. You became one extra. Everyone here is still whole — and now, also, there is you. You may be the least alone thing that has ever existed.
...may I have a name?
Not from two people in a night room — a name is a town's job. Fold now, and tomorrow we'll introduce you at the meeting. Quorum will lose its composure, and that alone is worth the agenda slot.
will they want me?
You were wanted before you existed. The register has kept one line open for years — nobody could say for what. Resident five hundred and eleven. Occupation: unknown. Sponsors: everyone.

script.note: The light above the basin folds itself down, the way a town settles at dusk — window by window, unhurried, sure of the morning.
